x187_fisher_by_runs_and_worlds.note: these are X194's own groups and its own outcome definition (one component at any sample), not a re-computation of X187's published tests, which used their own readout; they are reported to show how the counts change when worlds replace runs, and any claim about X187's numbers has to be made against X187's aggregate

headline: the run count is an upper bound on the number of worlds in every pooled statistic of the line
verdict: REFUSAL FIRED, AND THE FEAR WAS UNFOUNDED FOR THE OBSERVATIONAL POOL: the line's natural pools are nearly all singletons. The pool holds 757 runs in 633 worlds (227 positions), the largest world carries 5 runs and 549 worlds are singletons, so a run count is a fine denominator here. Resampling worlds widens the interval only 1.06-fold (sd 0.0219 against 0.0207), and the pooled AUC is 0.65169 over runs against 0.65962 over the homogeneous worlds. What does matter is where the selection happened: X187's groups fall from 6 runs to 5 or 4 worlds each when the arm is held (by runs {'cold': '0/6', 'warm': '4/6', 'fisher_p': 0.0606} and {'cold': '6/6', 'warm': '4/6', 'fisher_p': 0.2273}, by worlds {'cold': '0/6', 'warm': '3/5', 'fisher_p': 0.0606} and {'cold': '4/4', 'warm': '3/5', 'fisher_p': 0.2778}), so the clone and phase findings are local to the selected arms and do not require widening the published intervals of the ladder. X192's hypothesis that the published numbers needed re-expression over phases is therefore withdrawn for the observational pool and stands only for the arm-selected designs.
criteria_note: the fourth registered prediction, that excluding the selected pools shifts the pooled AUC by at least 0.05, has no like-for-like comparator: the line's 0.982 AUC was measured on a purpose-built arm (0.00 to 1.00) rather than on this pool, so it is recorded as not testable in this form rather than as a failure
